children: Wall Street ended Tuesday mixed as investors weighed geopolitical risks and a diplomatic calendar, even as technology shares pushed the Nasdaq Composite to a record high.

said geopolitics remained “front and center” with the United Nations General Assembly underway and President Donald Trump preparing to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington this week. The summit is expected to address trade and other contentious issues, with Reuters reporting that the leaders will meet Thursday at the White House.

Hecht also pointed to the November 3 U.S. midterm elections, noting that early voting has begun. He said historical trends have supported significant gains for the opposition party in midterm elections, although he noted divisions within Democrats could affect contests.
“Markets reflect geopolitical and economic landscapes that remain highly volatile,” Hecht stated. “Expect volatile periods in markets across all asset classes over the coming weeks,” he added.
Investors therefore face a backdrop shaped by international negotiations, domestic political developments, and continued uncertainty across financial markets.
